narr: Multiple upper disturbances moved across the region from the 12th through the 16th causing a rounds of strong to severe thunderstorms which produced numerous reports of damage, flooding, and high winds.
ev: The river gauge at Oberlin indicated the Calcasieu briefly exceeded bank full and flooded nearby fields and roads.
Water approached some homes in the Sulphur area with numerous streets flooded in Sulphur, Moss Bluff, and Lake Charles during the storm. Some road ways were closed as water became too deep.
Several streets around Crowley were reported flooded including portions of highway 13.
Street flooding was reported in New Iberia with some streets impassable.
A DD6 gauge on the Little River indicated that the stream flooded Holbrook Park and neighboring roadways.
A report of flooding north of Duson was received through MPING of flooding of streets and yards during the passing storm.
The DeRidder Police Department reported roads along Palmetto Creek flooded including Loftin, Hayes, and Graybow Roads.

A line of storms produced heavy rain around Lafayette flooding several roads. A report from MPING indicated some streets were closed with a video from social media showing roads and sidewalks flooded on the southwest side of the city.
The gauge WHTL1 on Cocodrie Bayou indicated the water level exceeded flood stage and flooded near by roads and fields.
The Allen Parish Sheriff's Department reported several street underwater and impassable from Oberlin to Mittie, and Oakdale.
Numerous roads were flooded in Jennings during the passing storm. A few vehicles were also reported stranded. Flooding was also reported in Hathaway and Elton.
